description:
From the fz-kdt.144 cold review (2026-09-02, d2a5f3510) -- the largest
finding of the arc close. callsite_dispatch.rs dispatch_from_callable_flow_
edges (~:484) builds PatternRows straight from flow.first_class_edges (the
fz-kdt.108 canonical cmp_tys order, which is a CONTENT order, not a safety
order) and calls pattern_dispatch_from_source; it never calls
routable_alternatives, so neither fz-kdt.143's drop (unroutable_
alternatives) nor fz-kdt.129/131's covering seat (specificity_order) runs on
a wrapper's member selection. specificity_order has exactly two callers,
both in callsite_dispatch.rs (:107 the callsite path, :1505 a gate).
MEASURED: 00277_enum_tier0_fixture, Enum.reverse(1..7//2, [:tail]) --
wrapper w2's selection for Enum.reduce/3#lambda@439-517/2 tests
  n8 empty_list() -> n6 list(int) -> n4 list(int | :tail) -> n2 list(int | :tail)
so the accumulator [1, :tail] passes list(int)'s head test and runs the body
compiled for [integer]. stdout is right on every door only because the
accumulator lane is ValueRef in both bodies (boxed element access -- the
fz-kdt.131 'correlation never proved', measured). The covering member exists
(x23/x24 keyed list(int | :tail)); it is seated second. Under
FZ_STRESS_PERMUTE_DISPATCH=wrappers:1/6/reverse the escape count is 0: the
settled order is the only escaping one (fz-kdt.147's shape on the list
axis). Reproducer: FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP=1 fz2 interp
fixtures2/00277_enum_tier0_fixture.fz 2>&1 >/dev/null | grep -c
'surface-membership escape'  -> 12 (after fz-kdt.144 lands).
CURE: member selection is a dispatch like any other -- route the wrapper's
members through routable_alternatives (drop + seat) with the member's
observable surface, and delete the direct row construction; the
fz-kdt.108 body_id weld (selection row index == member index) must be
re-derived from the seated order, not assumed. Acceptance: tripwire 0 on
00277 at settled AND under every wrappers:/arms: setting; the widened static
census (see the instrument ticket) green; canon movers classified; 0
behaviour movers on three doors.

comments.text: REPRODUCER IS LIVE AND PINNED (fz-kdt.144, 0889c0b3a): FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP=1 fz2 interp fixtures2/00277_enum_tier0_fixture.fz 2>&1 >/dev/null | grep -c 'surface-membership escape' -> 12. Each report names the value and the element that broke it: `value [1, :tail], element 1 = :tail is outside every clause the surface names` (4x), and the same for [3, 1, :tail] (element 2) and [5, 3, 1, :tail] (element 3). Measured invariance: 12 at the settled arrival and under arms:reverse and arms:1..6 -- the callsite arrival order does not touch it, the evidence that this is member SELECTION and not a callsite seat; 0 under wrappers:1, wrappers:6 and wrappers:reverse: the settled wrapper order is the only escaping order. Corpus-wide nothing else at the settled arrival. SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP_CENSUS pins all five rows (settled 12, arms:6 12, three wrapper settings 0), so the cure is red-first by construction: routing wrapper members through routable_alternatives must take the settled 12 to 0 without moving the wrapper rows off 0. Expect canon movers on 00277 -- classify them; 0 behaviour movers on three doors is the other half. Sequence after fz-kdt.178 (the widened static census is the second oracle).

CORRECTION from the fz-kdt.178 cold review (2026-09-03): the escaping wrappers on 00277 are w10, w11, w20 (4 members) and w13-w19 (11 members) -- TEN wrappers, 62 static covering-seat findings -- not w2, which holds s1 = [] / [{any,any}] / [] | [{any,any}] and escapes nowhere. The dynamic tripwire prints no wrapper id (value + element + predicate only), so "w2" was an inference never measured; its 12 escapes carry the test `lists {Empty, NonEmpty}, heads [ints cofinite]`, matching the [int] / [] | [int] members at those ten wrappers. Of the 62 static findings, 28 are pairs whose tests are DISJOINT at subject 0 (no value can satisfy both arms; covers's position-wise `all` reports them anyway -> fz-kdt.186), so this ticket's reachable reproducer is 34 seats across those wrappers plus 00420 4, enum_take_drop_split 4, enum_hof_three_distinct_closures 3 on the corpus. fz-kdt.178 lands a per-SITE allowance in the seat gate; this ticket retires it row by row. Also measured: selection findings are invariant under every arm seed (this is a wrapper-order axis), the fz-kdt.108 weld (outcomes[i].body_id == i) holds on every wrapper in the corpus, and the seated order IS the member-list order by construction -- so routing members through routable_alternatives must re-derive the weld from the seated order, exactly as the ticket says.

DATA POINT from the fz-kdt.183 cold review (2026-09-03): keying recursive activations on the list ELEMENT (183's prototype) retires this ticket's dynamic reproducer entirely -- 00277 surface-membership escapes 12 -> 0 at settled and under arms:6, enum_predicate_search 1 -> 0 -- because the members that used to differ only in a tail no test reads become distinct elements the test CAN read. That does not make member selection sound (the seat and drop still never run on it: a wrapper whose members differ elsewhere still seats by mint order), so this ticket stays; but its acceptance oracle changes with 183/124 and the reachable reproducer set must be re-measured after they land.

title: Construction-wrapper member selection bypasses the drop and the covering seat: dispatch_from_callable_flow_edges seats members in interner order
